_source: HeartOS/01_core_tables/nafs_states.md. The four canonical stations of the soul are Ammarah (12:53), Lawwamah (75:2), Mulhamah (91:7-8), and Mutmainnah (89:27-30).
_authentication_standard: All four Quran references are verified against the Mushaf: 12:53 (Ammarah — 'the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil'), 75:2 (Lawwamah — 'I swear by the self-reproaching soul'), 91:7-8 (Mulhamah — 'the soul at rest and proportioned, then He inspired it'), 89:27-30 (Mutmainnah — 'O soul at peace, return to your Lord'). These are the canonical Quranic anchors of the four-station taxonomy in the Islamic tradition. See HeartOS/GLOSSARY.md for the full description of each state.

nafs_states.Name: Ammarah
nafs_states.Description: The soul that commands evil — base desires dominate. The Quran says: 'Indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil — except those upon which my Lord has bestowed mercy.' (12:53)

nafs_states.Name: Lawwamah
nafs_states.Description: The self-reproaching soul. The Quran swears by it: 'And I swear by the self-reproaching soul.' (75:2) The default starting state for a new user.

nafs_states.Name: Mulhamah
nafs_states.Description: The inspired soul. The soul that has been inspired to distinguish good from evil and receives ilham from Allah. A rare and precious state.

nafs_states.Name: Mutmainnah
nafs_states.Description: The tranquil soul. The highest station attainable in this life. The Quran says: 'O soul at peace, return to your Lord, well-pleased and well-pleasing to Him.' (89:27-30)
